title: PM Review Decision
description: Machine-readable outcome of a single Claude Code task, written by automation/generate_decision_package.py to automation/review/review_decision.json. Every field has a single fixed meaning and is derived from structured inputs (task_meta.json fields, quality_checks.json check results) -- never from parsing free-form prose. Intended to be consumable by a CI system (e.g. GitHub Actions) with no human-in-the-loop text interpretation.

task_id.description: The Task ID this decision applies to, copied verbatim from task_meta.json.

status.description: PASS: no auto-stop flags were set and every executed quality check passed (skips do not count as failures). FAIL: no auto-stop flags were set but at least one quality check failed. BLOCKED: task_meta.json's `flags` array was non-empty (an Auto-Stop condition fired), OR `status_override` was explicitly set to BLOCKED. `status_override` in task_meta.json, if set, always wins over the derived value.

risk.description: Copied verbatim from task_meta.json's `risk` field. A human/Claude judgment call, never inferred (e.g. not derived from diff size or file count). Defaults to MEDIUM if task_meta.json omits it. Does not currently gate the pipeline -- it is informational, for a human or a future CI policy to act on.

blocked.description: True if and only if status == "BLOCKED". Provided as a separate boolean (rather than requiring a consumer to string-compare status) for simple CI gating.

next_task.description: PASS: task_meta.json's `next_task_id` field verbatim, or null if that field was not set (never guessed from the free-text `suggested_next_task`). FAIL: always the fixed pattern "REWORK-<task_id>", regardless of what next_task_id said -- a failed task's next step is fixing itself, not moving forward. BLOCKED: always null -- no next task can be determined until the blocker is resolved.

requires_human_approval.description: Always true. Fixed per PM OS rule: no implementation begins without explicit human approval, regardless of status. This automation layer never sets this to false and never acts on next_task_draft.md itself.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this decision was generated.

reason.description: One-line, deterministic explanation of how `status` was derived (e.g. which flags were present, which checks failed, or that status_override was used). For audit/traceability, not for parsing -- treat as a human-readable log line, not a structured field.
